scene.testo: In ancient Rome, your day started before the sun did. No coffee, no alarm clock, no snooze button. You got up in the dark, in the cold, and got dressed by feel. Within twenty minutes, you had to be standing outside a rich man's house.
Why? Because if you weren't there, you didn't eat that day. That's not an exaggeration. That was the system. For hundreds of years, this was daily life for hundreds of thousands of ordinary Romans.
We picture togas, marble, and emperors giving speeches. The reality was louder, dirtier, and stranger than any movie has ever shown you. And here's the part that breaks most people's brains.
The Romans did not have hours the way you do. So how did anyone know when to show up? What would you have done all day?

descrizione:
What did people in ancient Rome actually do all day? Forget the movies. Daily life in ancient Rome began in the dark, with a knock on the door and a long walk to a rich man's house just to earn the day's meal.

In this cartoon history video we explore the real Roman daily routine: the patron and client system, crowded apartments, noisy streets, bakers, markets and gamblers. It was louder, dirtier and stranger than any documentary on the Roman Empire has shown you.

Watch to find out how ordinary Romans survived, why the Romans did not have hours like we do, and what life was truly like in ancient Rome.
